In mathematics, the '''Chevalley–Iwahori–Nagata theorem''' states that if a [[linear algebraic group]] ''G'' is [[Group action (mathematics)|acting]] linearly on a finite-dimensional [[vector space]] ''V'', then the map from ''V''/''G'' to the [[Spectrum of a ring|spectrum]] of the ring of [[Invariant theory|invariant polynomials]] is an [[Group isomorphism|isomorphism]] if this ring is finitely generated and all [[Group action (mathematics)|orbits]] of ''G'' on ''V'' are [[closed set|closed]] {{harvs|last=Dieudonné|last2=Carrell|year1=1970|year2=1971|loc1=p.53|loc2=p.55}}. It is named after [[Claude Chevalley]], [[Nagayoshi Iwahori]], and [[Masayoshi Nagata]].
